conviction_note: Four guidance and positioning findings net to +0.9: a low bar and input costs no worse than when the guide was set, against a weak Idaho/PNW 2026 crop and a European crop that cuts both ways. I emit +0.5, 0.4 below the sum, because the long runs against record put demand and against a shareholder base that sold a beat-and-raise (-8.9% on 2026-04-01) and barely paid for a 40% EPS beat (+0.8% on 2026-07-24). The Q1 number itself should clear the company's flat-sales guide (+1%), but this name trades on the FY27 guide, not the quarter.
bar: Revenue: company guide is flat Q1 sales against Q1 FY26's $1,659.3M, with adj. EBITDA down low teens from $302.2M (~$257-269M) (https://www.tradingview.com/news/marketbeat:050ea40af094b:0-lamb-weston-q4-earnings-call-highlights/ ; base https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250930710677/en/Lamb-Weston-Reports-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Results-Reaffirms-Fiscal-Year-2026-Outlook). Consensus is $1.654-1.66B revenue and $0.58-0.59 EPS, from two agreeing sources (https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/29/lamb-weston-lw-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday.html ; https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/lamb-weston-stock-heads-into-earnings-after-target-cut/70196124). FY27 guide is $1.1-1.2B adj. EBITDA and $2.95-3.25 adj. EPS (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001679273/000167927326000024/a-lwx20260531xexx991fy26v2.htm). Bar is sourced, so no cap applies.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.29M shares at the 2026-08-31 FINRA settlement, 4.77 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/lw/short-interest). Ortex on 2026-09-30 puts it at 4.7% of free float, borrow cost 0.48%, availability 2,455% of SI, so the short is not crowded and offers no squeeze mechanism. Put/call ratio 2.08 is a 52-week high, two standard deviations above average (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution), and put volume rose 829% on 2026-09-18. The baseline has no usable chain, no skew value, and P/C OI 8.43 on only 66 contracts. The market's lean, read from put demand and the -20.7% 20-day run-up, is clearly bearish.

findings.finding: The fall's catalyst is Europe's crop (NEPG output -25%, Stephens' cut on FY27 procurement uncertainty), but the 2026 European contracts were priced 15-25% below last year and growers must fill them before selling spot. LW's CFO said in August that LW is 'covered' for European supply. Against that, the industry contracted fewer volumes and spot has jumped to EUR 200-240/t, so FY27 H2 (Jan-May 2027) does carry free-market exposure. Resolved net: slightly less bad than the narrative, not good.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide moves this stock: -25.9% on 2025-12-19 and -20.1% on 2024-12-19 (both December crop and guide resets), +16.3% on 2025-07-23 and +4.3% on 2025-09-30, when a Q1 reaffirmed the year.
findings.why_not_priced: Stephens' 2026-09-28 cut and the September slide treat European procurement cost as an open FY27 risk. If the contract buffer were priced, the stock would not have kept falling on European crop headlines through late September, and Stephens would not have cut on 'procurement cost uncertainty' for this fiscal year.
findings.independence: CFO quote that LW is covered for European supply, https://www.potatonewstoday.com/2026/08/16/lamb-weston-flags-price-risks-from-heat-impacted-potato-crop/ (2026-08-16). The counter-evidence is the spot surge, https://www.agrilinkage.com/post/europe-s-potato-shortfall-shows-how-acreage-and-weather-risks-can-compound, and LW's own July remark about a 'more pronounced reduction in contracted volumes across the industry'.

findings.finding: The North American 2026 crop, which feeds the segment that is about 2/3 of sales and nearly all EBITDA, is coming in short. A processor told Capital Press that Idaho yields are 'as bad as we've had in years', 50-60 sacks/acre below 2025, with low specific gravity and smaller size. PNW shippers report smaller size and lower volume. On 2026-08-12 LW had called its NA crop 'normal to slightly ahead of normal'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Crop and cost-driven guide resets were the two worst prints in the baseline: -25.9% (2025-12-19) and -20.1% (2024-12-19). The Q1 calls (Oct 2025, +4.3%) are where management first characterises the new crop.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell-side narrative into the print (Stephens 2026-09-28, the press) is entirely about Europe. The Idaho yield read was published 2026-09-29, after the Stephens note, and contradicts LW's own August NA crop description. If it were priced, previews would be cutting NA FY27 margin rather than international.
findings.independence: PNW report of smaller size and lower volume, https://www.thepacker.com/news/lower-potato-volume-brings-market-relief-pacific-northwest-shippers (snippet_only, 403 on fetch). It is an industry proxy, not an LW number; LW's NA contracted acreage is 'modestly higher', which partly offsets it.

findings.finding: The bar for the FY27 guide is already below the company's range: street FY27 EPS was $2.85 against the $2.95-3.25 guide on the day it was issued. Since then four analysts cut estimates and JPM ($52 to $46, 2026-09-30) and Stephens ($55 to $50) cut targets, so a trim to the low end or a modest cut is roughly what consensus already models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time a Q1 call reaffirmed into a depressed tape, the stock rose +4.3% (2025-09-30). A beat-and-raise into a weak tape still fell -8.9% (2026-04-01), so a low bar alone has not guaranteed a bid.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced, not a hidden fact. Its value is the asymmetry: with consensus below the guide's low end and puts at a 52-week high, only a cut below the street, not a cut to the low end, would be news. If the market expected only a low-end trim, put demand would not be at a two-standard-deviation extreme.
findings.independence: Target cuts and downward revisions: https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-stock-price-target-on-europe-concerns-93CH-4919969 and https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9104017/lw-maintained-by-jp-morgan-price-target-lowered-to-46

findings.finding: The input-cost risk management named as the driver of the guide's low end ('Middle East impacts on global input cost volatility through the first half') has not worsened since the guide. Brent settled near $97 on 2026-07-24 and was $97-100 on 2026-09-29/30. Soybean oil has fallen from a $0.797/lb June high into a 65-75c range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolates this line. Input-cost inflation was part of the margin concern behind the -8.9% on 2026-04-01.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews frame FY27 as getting worse since July, on crop. If the flat oil and edible-oil tape were priced, the September de-rating would have been attributed to crop alone, and the guide's low end would not still be read as a floor at risk.
findings.independence: Late-September prices from different sources: https://fortune.com/article/price-of-oil-09-29-2026/ and https://www.indexbox.io/blog/soybean-oil-futures-stay-rangebound-despite-cme-soybean-highs-and-crude-oil-above-100/. The company named the transmission itself on the Q4 call, https://www.tradingview.com/news/marketbeat:050ea40af094b:0-lamb-weston-q4-earnings-call-highlights/

outside_window.finding: Europe's 2026 spot surge (EUR 200-240/t) and the 25% smaller crop set up much higher 2027-crop contract prices, but also less European export overcapacity flooding LW's international markets. Both effects land in FY28 contracting and pricing, not on this print.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly long against a strongly bearish tape: -20.7% over 20 days, -37% from the 52-week high, record put demand. The negatives the market fears are mostly priced (a bar already below the guide's low end), and the one under-discussed negative is the NA crop, so the honest read is near zero, tilted slightly up.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 (caveat must reach the number): the European contract-buffer finding carried its own rebuttal (reduced industry contracting, spot surge), so I resolved it to one net sign and cut it from +0.5 to +0.3.

Rule 5 (an industry proxy is a hypothesis until the company says it): the Idaho/PNW yield finding rests on an unnamed processor and state-level reporting, not an LW number, and LW's own August view was 'normal', so I cut it from -2.0 to -1.2.

Rule 7 and the baseline guidance (a long against bid puts needs a reason): the low-bar/positioning finding is close to 'it is cheap'; its consensus source dates from guide day, and low SI means no squeeze mechanism, so I cut it from +2.0 to +1.2.
Rule 5 again on input costs: I kept the finding because the company itself named the transmission, but cut it from +0.8 to +0.6 because it is still macro inference.

Rule 3 / conviction note: I emit expected_move +0.5, visibly below the +0.9 sum, because the lean runs against the put positioning and against this holder base's habit of selling beats. Rule 1 left print_vs_bar at +1.0 and decoupled it from the move.

Left standing: the bar sourcing (company guide plus two agreeing estimates, so no cap) and all resolves_by dates (2026-10-06, inside the window); the FY28 European pricing item stays in outside_window.
